text:
maria: Customer GammaApps (private VPC) reporting a spike of 504s and mTLS auth failures following our cert rotation last night. Ticket GAM-842. Started around 02:15 UTC, affects a subset of backend nodes.

jake: Can you paste a sample client repro (curl/openssl) and the rotator run id? Also which VPC cluster?

maria: Customer sent this from their ops team:
```
openssl s_client -connect api.private.gamma.internal:443 -servername api.private.gamma.internal -showcerts
---
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = GammaRoot, CN = Gamma Root CA
verify error:num=19:self signed certificate in certificate chain
---
```
They said the failures started right after our rotator job around 02:13-02:16 UTC. Rotator id they saw in audit: rdr-rot-20260316-77. VPC cluster: vc-gamma-3 (10.11.5.x).

tom: Quick checklist: 1) confirm full chain bundle uploaded to rotator 2) check per-node cert on 10.11.5.* 3) check whether customer uses fingerprint pinning.

maria: Customer confirmed they pinned the leaf cert fingerprint in their terraform provisioning (they have an internal policy). They didn't pick up the new fingerprint. They forwarded an inventory command they ran: 
```
echo | openssl s_client -connect 10.11.5.12:443 -servername api.private.gamma.internal 2>/dev/null \
  | sed -n '/BEGIN CERTIFICATE/,/END CERTIFICATE/p' \
  | openssl x509 -noout -fingerprint
# output -> SHA1:AB:CD:EF:12:34:... (old fingerprint)
```
So node 10.11.5.12 is still serving the old cert.

jake: That matches my suspicion — one node didn't reload the new bundle. Any HAProxy / proxy logs showing reload errors?\
maria: We pulled the rotator logs (from customer-facing console) and saw the rotator uploaded the bundle but there was a reload failure on that instance. From our side we see a rotator worker error at 02:14:23: `reload failed: too many open files` on node 10.11.5.12.

eva: I can confirm in infra: rotator run rdr-rot-20260316-77 -> status: partial-reload-failure. One worker hit fd leak that prevented `s6` from restarting haproxy on that host. The other two nodes rotated fine. I can force a reload now.\
maria: Customer is asking for mitigation steps and ETA, also they mentioned unexpected billing for retries during the outage. They want a quick workaround they can apply on their side.

tom: Mitigation options (short-term):
- Force haproxy reload on node 10.11.5.12 (infra)
- Or temporarily accept old fingerprint on their side (not ideal)
- Or have customer update pinned fingerprint to new one immediately after we confirm new cert on all nodes
I also recommend we add a rotator post-rotate check: verify per-node cert fingerprint matches expected bundle and alert if any node still serves old cert. Filing infra-ticket now.

jake: To reproduce locally for triage: run `openssl s_client -connect 10.11.5.12:443 -servername api.private.gamma.internal -showcerts`, confirm fingerprint mismatch, tail `/var/log/rotator/20260316-77.log` for the `reload failed` entry.

maria: I told the customer we can force the reload and asked for permission to run it. They granted permission. Eva, please proceed.

eva: Forced reload executed at 03:02 UTC on 10.11.5.12. Post-reload check: `openssl x509 -noout -fingerprint` now returns new fingerprint on that node. Customer ran their tests and reports handshakes succeeding. They still saw transient 504s during the window while one node was serving old certs.

rotator-bot: Rotator run rdr-rot-20260316-77 status update: partial-reload-failure -> manual-reload-done-by-oncall. Logs: /var/log/rotator/20260316-77.log (fd leak trace present).

jake: Action items: 1) Eva to open incident PR (root cause: fd leak in rotator worker causing partial reload) 2) Tom to add fingerprint post-rotate verification check + alert 3) Support to inform billing team about transient retries and customer complaint (GAM-842).

tom: Filed infra ticket: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues/5123 (add post-rotate per-node fingerprint verification).

maria: Customer confirmed resolution on their side and will keep us posted if they see any more auth failures. Marking the thread as resolved from support perspective for now. :thumbsup:

eva: I'll include the rotator fd-leak logs in the incident ticket and schedule a follow-up rollout test in staging to avoid recurrence.

maria: Thanks all — summarizing for the postmortem and customer notes.
